analysis:
Examined three benchmark-only (ProviderBenchmark target) source changes, all of which appear to be API-adaptation edits following an upstream mlx-swift-lm bump.

1. MTPProductionSession.swift:115 (head): Gemma4AssistantDraftModel is now qualified as MLXLLM.Gemma4AssistantDraftModel. This is a name disambiguation only. Load behavior is unchanged: cache-only loading from the local assistantDirectory, no download. The prefix-cache kill switch at line 226 (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 for benchmark engines) is unchanged, so the T-041 posture is unaffected.

2. ModelBenchmark.swift:256 (head): the switch now handles a new Generation case, .rejectedToolCall, alongside .toolCall; both are ignored in the benchmark. There is no output or exposure change.

3. ThroughputSweep.swift:127/219/224/227/237: newCache(parameters:) is now throwing, and errors propagate via try. This makes the benchmark fail closed on cache construction errors rather than silently proceeding, so there is no security regression.

None of these files touch the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), keys (A-003), the prefix-cache SSD tier (T-041), or consumer data paths.

Integration questions (outside this batch): the upstream dependency bump introduces .rejectedToolCall and a throwing newCache. Production serving paths in ProviderCore, such as EngineV2Bridge and tool-call handling, should be checked for two things:
- that rejected tool calls are not emitted to consumers as plaintext or unencrypted output (T-008);
- that newCache throw paths fail closed and release any KV budget they reserved (T-041 staging reservations).

Those files were not supplied to this pass.
